To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Sulina-Sahalin littoral cell is in unfavourable sediment status, the coast is vulnerable to short term extreme event (especially storms) and the main solution to deal with this situation is to restore the sediment circulation in the littoral cell, by artificial nourishment.

the coastal area between Sahalin and Sulina branches is vulnerable to erosion and to the extreme events; the main threats for this coastal zone are related to the lack of sediments and to the vulnerability of the coastline to the extreme events (storms); the main solution to deal with the threats is to restore the natural sediment budget by the transfer of strategic sediments from two reservoirs to the central part of Sulina – Sahalil littoral cell.

the Sulina – Sahalina littoral cell is sediment-starved, vulnerable to extreme events and that artificial nourishment of the central part of this cell, using sediments from strategic sediment reservoirs, is the best way to deal with erosion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the EUROSION FP5 concepts and the development of a coastal management methodology for the Sulina – Sahalim littoral cell.

the following issues: (i) the application of CONSCIENCE Framework in a coastal environment; (ii) the application of the EUROSION FP5 project concepts; (iii) the development of a working methodology to deal with coastal erosion problems.

the development of a sustainable coastal management strategy for the Danube Delta, which will be implemented in a pilot project, and will be used as an example for the development of a strategy at the national level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CONSCIENCE approach and the related methodology can be successfully applied to coastal management problems, especially when dealing with erosion.

the CONSCIENCE Framework, methodology and tools are suitable to be applied in the Danube Delta coastal management and to be further developed in order to deal with the coastal problems of the Danube River Delta.
the CONSCIENCE Framework can provide a good working methodology for coastal studies and management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a sustainable coastal management is possible if the local authorities and stakeholders are aware of the threats, are able to identify them and to propose solutions to deal with them.
we have a clear understanding of the coastal processes and their evolution, as well as a good understanding of the problems and solutions for this particular environment.
the CONSCIENCE experience is a good starting point for a sustainable coastline management in the Danube Delta coastal area.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coastal managers need to be aware of the sediment dynamics in the coastal area, to identify the sediment sources and sinks and to develop a sediment management strategy for the coastal zone, in order to maintain the coastal resilience.
the coastal managers should take into account all the factors affecting the coastal environment, including natural and human induced ones.
the coastal managers should be able to identify and understand coastal problems, as well as propose solutions for them.
